chapter: Life in New York in the 1940s
title: Pot and wine versus heroin, which came with bebop
summary: Edison says earlier musicians only used pot and wine, and heavy drugs arrived with the bebop era, partly through imitating Parker.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: And there was no drinking, really?
No. If you did, you drank just a little glass of sweet wine, something like that. We used to get the port wine because it was so cheap. You could get a gallon of it for about 35 cents, you know.
So you'd get pretty high?
Yeah.
But it would be harmless, really.

Yeah. That's all you'd get, you know. And the whiskey, naturally a lot of the guys, lot of musicians drink the whiskey. But there was no dope connected with it, you know. Not the heroin and cocaine. All that was --
Did that grow out of the same people, the pot peddlers, you know?
No, no.
It was a different --

Different thing. Different thing. Because when the heavy stuff became popular in New York, that seemed to make its appearance around the be-bop era. The bee-bop era, you know, because -- well, it's always something got to go with an era, you know, something.
Then it became a fashion?
Yeah. Yeah, it -- you know, Charlie Parker was such a fantastic musician. And he created -- he turned the prospective of all saxophone players all around,
you know.
Yeah.
He ruined many would-be good saxophone players, had they just gone for themselves, you know.
Because it was too difficult for the average person.
Oh, sure. And they figured if Charlie Parker could play that way under the influence of what he used, you know, that they could do it, too. So that spoiled a couple of them short, you know.

And, of course, pot never hurt anybody. You know, they never -- they still haven't proved it was a dope of any kind, you know. But that, the other phase of narcotics such as the heroin, the cocaine, that's just absolutely -- that's taken a lot of good musicians away from here.
Yeah, yeah.
And it's just too bad that people can't think for themselves. And they can see where it's killing somebody and they'll go right on, keep on doing it, you know -- their best friends.
